def-simulation-gradient-objective-and-pa:
## Definition

Fix a finite dimension $d\ge1$, an open set $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, and a probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal F,P)$. A simulation payoff is a jointly measurable map $H:\Theta\times\Omega\to\mathbb R$ such that $H(\theta,\cdot)$ is integrable for each $\theta\in\Theta$. Its objective is
$J(\theta):=\mathbb E[H(\theta,\cdot)].$
A payoff-oracle call at $\theta$ returns an integrable real random variable $Y(\theta)$ with $\mathbb E[Y(\theta)]=J(\theta)$. Two calls may use the same random input or different random inputs; their joint law is part of the chosen coupling. A single oracle call is one function evaluation, regardless of the cost of its internal simulation.
alg-two-evaluation-spsa-gradient-estimat:
## Definition

Input a dimension $d\ge1$, $\theta\in\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, a scalar $c>0$, a payoff oracle from [[def-simulation-gradient-objective-and-payoff-oracle]], and a random vector $\Delta=(\Delta_1,\ldots,\Delta_d)$ whose coordinates are independent, symmetric about zero, and nonzero almost surely. Require $\theta+c\Delta,\theta-c\Delta\in\Theta$ almost surely.

1. Draw one $\Delta$.
2. Call the oracle once at $\theta+c\Delta$ and once at $\theta-c\Delta$, obtaining $Y^+$ and $Y^-$.
3. If either call fails or a perturbation is outside $\Theta$, return that failure status. Otherwise return
   $\widehat G_i(\theta):=\frac{Y^+-Y^-}{2c\Delta_i},\qquad i=1,\ldots,d.$

The same numerator supplies all $d$ coordinates, so one estimator uses exactly two oracle calls independently of $d$. The definition does not assert unbiasedness, finite variance, or convergence of an update rule.
def-coupled-simulation-finite-difference:
## Definition

For a scalar objective $J:\Theta\to\mathbb R$, a direction $v\in\mathbb R^d$, a step $h>0$, and a common simulation input $Z$, the coupled central-difference estimator is
$D_{h,v}^{\mathrm{coup}}:=\frac{H(\theta+hv,Z)-H(\theta-hv,Z)}{2h},$
provided both perturbed parameters lie in $\Theta$. The two outputs use the same $Z$; this choice fixes their joint law and hence their covariance. The estimator's variance is not asserted to be smaller for every coupling.
def-pathwise-simulation-gradient-estimat:
## Definition

Use [[def-simulation-gradient-objective-and-payoff-oracle]] and write $J(\theta)=\mathbb E[H(\theta,Z)]$ using one fixed random input $Z$ whose law does not depend on $\theta$. If, for almost every input, the map $\theta\mapsto H(\theta,Z)$ is differentiable, its pathwise (or reparameterized) gradient estimator is
$G_{\mathrm{pw}}(\theta,Z):=D_\theta H(\theta,Z).$
When $H(\theta,Z)=h(T(\theta,Z),\theta)$, with differentiable $T$ and $h$, the chain rule gives
$G_{\mathrm{pw}}=D_xh(T(\theta,Z),\theta)D_\theta T(\theta,Z)+\partial_\theta h(T(\theta,Z),\theta).$
The estimator differentiates the simulated outcome while holding the same random input fixed. This definition alone does not assert that its expectation equals $\nabla J(\theta)$.

prop-coupled-simulation-difference-varia:
## Statement

Let $Y^+$ and $Y^-$ be square-integrable real simulation outputs with any specified joint law, and let $h>0$. The central-difference estimator $D=(Y^+-Y^-)/(2h)$ satisfies
$\operatorname{Var}(D)=\frac{\operatorname{Var}(Y^+)+\operatorname{Var}(Y^-)-2\operatorname{Cov}(Y^+,Y^-)}{4h^2}.$
The formula applies in particular when the two outputs use common random numbers as in [[def-coupled-simulation-finite-difference-estimator]]. Positive covariance reduces this variance relative to independent outputs with the same marginals; coupling alone does not guarantee positive covariance.

thm-spsa-gradient-bias-is-second-order:
## Statement

Assume AC for the conditional-expectation interface. Let $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open, $\theta\in\Theta$, and $f:\Theta\to\mathbb R$ be $C^3$. For every permitted $\Delta$ and $0<c\le c_0$, assume the segment $\{\theta+t\Delta:|t|\le c\}$ lies in an open set $V_{c,\Delta}\subseteq\Theta$ on which $\|D^3 f(y)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le M_3$, where the operator norm is the supremum of $|D^3f[u,v,w]|$ over unit vectors $u,v,w$. Let $\Delta_1,\ldots,\Delta_d$ be independent, symmetric about zero, and nonzero almost surely, with
$\mathbb E|\Delta_j|<\infty,\qquad \mathbb E|\Delta_i|^{-1}<\infty,\qquad q_i:=\mathbb E\!\left[\frac{\|\Delta\|_2^3}{|\Delta_i|}\right]<\infty.$
Assume the two oracle outputs in [[alg-two-evaluation-spsa-gradient-estimator]] satisfy $\mathbb E[Y^\pm\mid\Delta]=f(\theta\pm c\Delta)$ and
$\mathbb E\!\left[\frac{|Y^+-f(\theta+c\Delta)|+|Y^--f(\theta-c\Delta)|}{|\Delta_i|}\right]<\infty$
for every $i$. Then
$\left|\mathbb E[\widehat G_i(\theta)]-\partial_i f(\theta)\right|\le \frac{M_3 c^2}{6}q_i,\qquad \left\|\mathbb E[\widehat G(\theta)]-\nabla f(\theta)\right\|_2\le\frac{M_3c^2}{6}\left(\sum_{i=1}^d q_i^2\right)^{1/2}.$
thm-spsa-gradient-has-inverse-step-varia:
## Statement

Assume AC. At a current history $\mathcal F$, let $c>0$, let $\Delta_i\ne0$ almost surely, and use the two-evaluation estimator from [[alg-two-evaluation-spsa-gradient-estimator]]. Suppose the weighted conditional second moment is bounded:
$\mathbb E\!\left[\left(|Y^+|^2+|Y^-|^2\right)\sum_{i=1}^d|\Delta_i|^{-2}\,\middle|\,\mathcal F\right]\le B$
almost surely, with deterministic $B<\infty$. Then
$\mathbb E[\|\widehat G\|_2^2\mid\mathcal F]\le\frac{B}{2c^2},\qquad \operatorname{Var}(\widehat G\mid\mathcal F)\le\frac{B}{2c^2},$
where the vector conditional variance is the sum of coordinate conditional variances as in [[def-stochastic-gradient-oracle-and-unconstrained-update]].
thm-spsa-stochastic-approximation-has-st:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$, bounded below by a finite $f_{\inf}$, and have an $L$-Lipschitz gradient. Let $(\mathcal F_k)$ be a filtration, let $x_k$ be $\mathcal F_k$-measurable, and let $G_k$ be the output of the SPSA estimator in [[alg-two-evaluation-spsa-gradient-estimator]], measurable with respect to $\mathcal F_{k+1}$. At each iteration, draw $\Delta_k$ and the simulator random inputs freshly and independently of $\mathcal F_k$; the two paired calls may share their random input. Suppose $\Delta_k$ has a fixed perturbation law, the calls satisfy $\mathbb E[Y_k^\pm\mid\mathcal F_k,\Delta_k]=f(x_k\pm c_k\Delta_k)$, and their conditional bias and weighted second moments give, almost surely,
$\|\mathbb E[G_k\mid\mathcal F_k]-\nabla f(x_k)\|_2\le Bc_k^2,\qquad \operatorname{Var}(G_k\mid\mathcal F_k)\le Vc_k^{-2},\qquad \|\nabla f(x_k)\|_2\le G,$
with deterministic $B,V,G<\infty$, and $c_k\in(0,1]$. The bias and variance hypotheses are supplied, for example, by the bounds of [[thm-spsa-gradient-bias-is-second-order]] and [[thm-spsa-gradient-has-inverse-step-variance-bound]] when their smoothness and weighted-moment conditions hold at each history.

For deterministic $\alpha_k>0$, update $x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha_kG_k$. Assume $X_k:=f(x_k)-f_{\inf}$ is nonnegative, adapted, and integrable at each $k$, and
$\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty,\qquad c_k\longrightarrow0,\qquad \sum_k\alpha_k c_k^2<\infty,\qquad \sum_k\frac{\alpha_k^2}{c_k^2}<\infty.$
Then $X_k$ converges almost surely,
$\sum_k\alpha_k\|\nabla f(x_k)\|_2^2<\infty\quad\text{almost surely},\qquad \liminf_{k\to\infty}\|\nabla f(x_k)\|_2=0\quad\text{almost surely}.$
This conclusion is a stationary-limit-point statement; it does not assert convergence to a minimizer or convergence of the full gradient sequence.
thm-discrete-sde-adjoint-gradient-interc:
## Statement

Let $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open, fix $\theta_0\in\Theta$, and choose an open ball $U$ with $\theta_0\in U\subseteq\Theta$. Let $d,m\ge1$, let $N\ge0$ be a finite integer, let the states lie in $\mathbb R^m$, and let $\xi=(\xi_0,\ldots,\xi_N)$ collect fixed simulation inputs on one probability space. The maps are $u_0:\Theta\times E_0\to\mathbb R^m$, $\Psi_k:\mathbb R^m\times\Theta\times E_{k+1}\to\mathbb R^m$, $\ell_k:\mathbb R^m\times\Theta\to\mathbb R$, and $\phi:\mathbb R^m\times\Theta\to\mathbb R$. Gradients of scalar functions are columns; $D_u\Psi_k$ is an $m\times m$ Jacobian and $D_\theta\Psi_k$ is an $m\times d$ Jacobian. Let
$u_0=u_0(\theta,\xi_0),\qquad u_{k+1}=\Psi_k(u_k,\theta,\xi_{k+1})\quad(0\le k<N).$
Assume the displayed step data maps are jointly measurable in all their arguments and, outside one probability-zero set, are continuously differentiable in their state and parameter variables on $U$. Define
$F_N(\theta,\xi):=\phi(u_N,\theta)+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\ell_k(u_k,\theta),\qquad J_N(\theta):=\mathbb E[F_N(\theta,\xi)].$
Assume $F_N(\theta,\xi)$ is integrable for every $\theta\in U$, and that there is a nonnegative integrable random variable $M$ with $\|\nabla_\theta F_N(\theta,\xi)\|_2\le M$ for all $\theta\in U$ almost surely, while $\mathbb E\|\nabla_\theta F_N(\theta_0,\xi)\|_2^2<\infty$. Put $S_0=D_\theta u_0$, propagate
$S_{k+1}=D_u\Psi_k\,S_k+D_\theta\Psi_k,$
and define reverse variables by
$p_N=\nabla_u\phi(u_N,\theta),\qquad p_k=\nabla_u\ell_k(u_k,\theta)+(D_u\Psi_k)^\mathsf T p_{k+1}.$
Then the discrete adjoint integrand
$\Gamma_N=\nabla_\theta\phi+S_0^\mathsf T p_0+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\left(\nabla_\theta\ell_k+(D_\theta\Psi_k)^\mathsf T p_{k+1}\right)$
satisfies $\nabla J_N(\theta_0)=\mathbb E[\Gamma_N(\theta_0,\xi)]$.

For a family of discretizations indexed by $h$, if each discrete objective satisfies the preceding pathwise interchange hypotheses, $\mathbb E\|\Gamma_h(\theta_0)-\Gamma(\theta_0)\|_2\to0$, and the continuous-limit objective has derivative $\nabla J(\theta_0)=\mathbb E[\Gamma(\theta_0)]$ under the same pathwise interchange conditions, then $\nabla J_h(\theta_0)\to\nabla J(\theta_0)$. This conclusion gives no rate unless a quantitative bound on $\mathbb E\|\Gamma_h(\theta_0)-\Gamma(\theta_0)\|_2$ is also supplied. Euler–Maruyama is the special case $\Psi_k(u,\theta,\Delta W_k)=u+b(u,\theta)h_k+\sigma(u,\theta)\Delta W_k$, with $\Delta W_k$ the simulated Brownian increment.
